Translate the following Python 3 code to GNU C++11 code. The code reads and writes I/O from the console. Your translated code should have the exact same functionality as the given code, meaning that it should have the same output for any given input.

n, m = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
import bisect
partA, partB = [], []
mid_point = n // 2

def get_sums1(i, total=0):
    if i == mid_point:
        partA.append(total)
    else:
        get_sums1(i + 1, (total + a[i]) % m)
        get_sums1(i + 1, total)

def get_sums2(i, total=0):
    if i == n:
        partB.append(total)
    else:
        get_sums2(i + 1, (total + a[i]) % m)
        get_sums2(i + 1, total)

get_sums1(0)
get_sums2(mid_point)

best_sum = 0
for val in partB:
    index = bisect.bisect_left(partA, m - val)
    if index > 0:
        candidate = partA[index - 1] + val
        if candidate > best_sum:
            best_sum = candidate
print(best_sum)
